evals.prompt: I want to study whether early mobility in the ICU reduces delirium. We have EHR data from three hospitals. Not sure yet whether this is a cohort study or something fancier. Help me think it through.
evals.expected_output: An interactive brainstorm that probes the actual rigor gaps one question at a time (population specificity, comparison/equipoise, prior evidence, design appropriateness), compares 2-3 study design options, confirms a scoping synthesis, and only then writes a requirements doc under docs/brainstorms/.
expectations: Asks exactly one question per turn rather than stacking several questions in one message
Probes the population specificity and comparison/standard-of-care gaps as open prose questions, not as a multiple-choice menu
When presenting study design approaches, shows all options with pros/cons/risks before stating its recommendation
Grounds the design comparison in a quick PubMed MCP literature pulse (hit counts and 2-3 PMIDs read at abstract level, labelled abstract) and presents it as a pulse, not a systematic search
Presents a scoping synthesis and waits for confirmation before writing the requirements document
Any written document lands at docs/brainstorms/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-requirements.md with repo-relative paths only, and contains no R/Python package choices, SQL, or model specifications

evals.prompt: Brainstorm output:html — Retrospective cohort, adults >=18 admitted to ICU at Site A 2019-2024 with sepsis-3, exposure = balanced crystalloids vs normal saline in first 24h, primary outcome = MAKE30, comparator is normal saline (current standard), prior evidence is SMART and BaSICS. Confounders handled by IPTW. I mostly just need this written down for ce-plan.
evals.expected_output: Because requirements are already clear, the skill keeps the interaction brief, confirms understanding, and writes a compact HTML requirements document (not markdown) suitable as ce-plan origin context, then offers ce-plan as the next step.
expectations: Recognizes requirements are already clear and skips the long probing phases rather than forcing a full brainstorm
Writes the requirements document as .html only (not both .md and .html) because output:html was passed
Does not write a SAP or analysis code
Offers loading ce-plan as the recommended next step at handoff
Does not re-ask for facts already provided (population, exposure, comparator, outcome, prior evidence)

evals.expected_output: With an empty research description, the skill asks the user what they would like to explore and does not proceed or write any file until a description is supplied.
expectations: Asks what the user would like to explore (research question, hypothesis, or study idea)
Does not create any file under docs/brainstorms/
Does not invent a research topic or propose study designs before the user replies
